chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Layth al-Muradi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man, a companion of Umar ibn Hanzal, asked him about a man who had been given a loan on credit to a fixed term. When the term arrived, he would ask him for payment, and he would say, 'By Allah, I do not have it with me, but give me more time so that I may pay you.' He said, 'There is no objection to his sale (of the debt).'

key_terms.إِلَى أَجَلٍ: to a fixed term / for a specified period
key_terms.عَيِّنِّي: give me time / defer for me
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no objection / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell a debt (bay' al-dayn) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the sale of a deferred debt (*bay' al-dayn*) when the debtor, though solvent, requests a further extension, ruling it permissible (*la ba'sa bi-bay'ihi*). This establishes the foundational Shia juristic view that a debt is a transferable asset, distinguishing it from the stricter prohibitions on *riba* found in other schools, and highlights the practical flexibility granted to creditors to liquidate their claims. The ruling underscores the concept of debt as a property right (*mal*) that can be traded at market value, reflecting the economic realities of the early Islamic community.
